title: U.S. House · Missouri's 6th District
area: Northern Missouri, stretching from the Kansas City area's northern suburbs across rural north Missouri to the Iowa border.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Sam Graves, first elected in 2000, retired from public office and did not appear on the August 4, 2026 Republican primary ballot. Chris Stigall defeated four other Republicans (Jim Ingram, Cody Oshel, Nathanael Schultz and Nathan Willett) in that primary. Josh Smead won a three-candidate Democratic primary over Matthew Levine and Scot Pondelick. Andy Maidment advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary. The Cook Political Report rated the district R+13 for the 2026 cycle.

candidates.name: Chris Stigall
candidates.ballotNote: Won a five-candidate August 4, 2026 Republican primary for this open seat

summary.text: Chris Stigall is the Republican nominee for the open Missouri 6th District seat. A conservative talk radio host in Kansas City and Philadelphia who once worked as a field representative in Rep. Sam Graves's office, he has not held elected office. His campaign describes support for President Trump's agenda on immigration, taxes, agriculture, gun rights and opposition to abortion.

background.text: Born January 5, 1977, in Richmond, Missouri (Ray County); according to his campaign website, his family later moved to Clay County, where he attended North Kansas City schools and graduated from Oak Park High School.
Earned a degree in broadcasting from Northwest Missouri State University, where he covered news for KXCV/KRNW, according to his campaign website.

Began in conservative talk radio in the early 2000s, then briefly served as a field representative and deputy communications director in Rep. Sam Graves's office before returning to radio on KCMO in Kansas City in 2006.

According to Wikipedia, hosted the morning show on WPHT in Philadelphia from 2011 to 2019 and launched a nationally syndicated morning show on the Salem Radio Network in January 2025; his career as a radio host has centered on conservative politics.

According to his campaign website, he has received the Phyllis Schlafly Truth in Journalism Award and the Clay County Republican Central Committee's Man of the Year award, and served as a board member of Liberty USO.

Entered the 2026 race for the open 6th District seat after Rep. Sam Graves, who has held it since 2001, announced he would not seek reelection; Graves endorsed him, and he won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Kansas City Council member Nathan Willett.

KCUR reports he has not held elected office and has said he would not hold the seat as long as Graves did; President Trump has called him a "great friend" but, as of KCUR's guide, had not made an official endorsement.

According to his campaign website, he and his wife Christine, who have three children, live in Holt, Missouri, attend Kearney First Baptist Church, and support school choice through the Herzog Foundation.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists the Second Amendment, rural healthcare, life, taxes, agriculture, cryptocurrency/financial freedom, and immigration/the SAVE Act as his core campaign issues.

positions.summary: Says the Second Amendment "is not negotiable" and he will oppose efforts to restrict gun rights through federal overreach.

Says he is "proudly pro-life" and will oppose taxpayer funding for abortion while supporting efforts to protect "innocent life," though he notes abortion policy is increasingly decided at the state level.
Supports making President Trump's tax cuts permanent and opposes raising taxes on families, farmers and small businesses.

Supports securing the border, finishing the border wall, ending catch-and-release policies, deporting people with criminal records who are in the country illegally, and the SAVE Act's citizenship voting requirement.
Supports President Trump's efforts to expand market access and strengthen domestic food production for farmers, without a direct statement on general tariff policy.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey completed and no independent biography found on Ballotpedia; positions are drawn entirely from his campaign website as reproduced by Ballotpedia. Has not previously held elected office, so has no official governmental record.

candidates.name: Josh Smead

summary.text: Josh Smead is the Democratic nominee for the open Missouri 6th District seat. A licensed architect and small-business owner from Liberty, Missouri, he has not held elected office and is campaigning on revitalizing rural north Missouri and term limits.

background.text: Graduated from Harrisonburg High School, earned a bachelor's degree from James Madison University in 2012 and a graduate degree from Iowa State University in 2016, according to Ballotpedia.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as working as an architect and general contractor.
Describes himself as a licensed architect and small-business owner who runs a local architecture and development firm with his wife in Liberty, Missouri; he is a father of four.
Won the Democratic primary for the 6th District on August 4, 2026; KCUR reports he has not previously held office.

Told St. Louis Public Radio that he decided to run in large part to help Democrats take back the U.S. House; KCUR notes the last time a Democrat held the seat was in 2001, under a different district configuration.

priorities.text: Family: says Missouri should be the best place in the country to raise a family, with safe communities, strong schools, affordable healthcare and local economies that work for everyday people.
Liberty/limited government: says he'll fight for term limits, defend the Constitution, and reduce red tape and federal overreach that he says chokes opportunity for small businesses.
Rural revitalization: says north Missouri needs a "generational investment" in infrastructure, from schools and roads to bridges, to restore the region's economic vibrancy.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Andy Maidment
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary

summary.text: Andy Maidment is the Libertarian Party nominee for the open Missouri 6th District seat. A military veteran and information technology professional, he describes himself as not a politician and is campaigning on limiting the federal government.

background.text: Born in West Columbia, South Carolina; according to his campaign website, he has lived in Missouri since age twelve, and Ballotpedia lists Park Hill High School as his high school.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history, with a minor in economics according to his campaign website, from Missouri State University in 2007.

Served in the U.S. Army from 2000 to 2004 and the U.S. Army National Guard from 2004 to 2021, according to Ballotpedia; his campaign website cites 21 years of service in the Army and Missouri National Guard.
Works as an information technology and cybersecurity professional, and describes himself as a father.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for the 6th District in 2022 and 2024, losing to Rep. Sam Graves both times.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, or other public statements of positions found.
